uncited: Multiple scattering approximations address the computational intractability of full volumetric path tracing by estimating the contribution of light undergoing two or more scattering events within participating media.
While [Single and multiple scattering](35-single-and-multiple-scattering.md) defines the physical interactions, this family focuses on efficient estimation strategies.

Unlike [Single Scattering Approximations](5340-single-scattering-approximations.md), which ignore higher-order bounces, these methods approximate the global illumination component, trading physical rigor for performance or artistic control.

They differ from [Radiative Transfer and Integral Equation Solvers](3853-radiative-transfer-and-integral-equation-solvers.md) by often employing stochastic or semi-analytic shortcuts rather than solving the full integro-differential equation deterministically.
All methods in this family operate on the principle that the total radiance $L$ is the sum of single-scattering ($L_1$) and multiple-scattering ($L_{\ge 2}$) contributions.
The core challenge is evaluating the in-scattering integral for higher-order bounces without infinite recursion.
